release_rule: Do not change the version to 2.0.0 until every blocking stage below passes on the same source and artifacts intended for release.
semantic_mismatch_policy: Preserve every CPU-vs-GPU mismatch. Run a second fresh CPU world against the CPU reference as a repeatability control before attributing it. Do not normalize generated UUIDs or other semantic NBT fields to force equality.

production_worldgen_gpu_integration.note: GPU kernel/backend components alone do not prove the vanilla terrain generator calls them, adopts verified values, or preserves save/reload semantics. Full density graph, fluid pressure/surface, feature placement, lighting and save computation are not GPU-ported.

stages.evidence: Python standard-library semantic/worldgen tests 19/19 and movement-gate source tests 4/4 passed locally; no server or bots launched.
stages.acceptance: Semantic decoding/comparison, strict-versus-verified-exact telemetry gates, immutable matrix references, and 20% server-observed movement gating pass their isolated source tests.

Finish production Gradle suites/build, compile the updated benchmark plugin and standalone worldgen probe against the immutable candidate, then record candidate SHA-256. Verify the probe writes raw per-tick CSV and generate/reload p50/p95/p99/max MSPT and start-interval statistics, >50/>100ms tick counts and measured TPS.
Verify pending worldgen futures, including a continuation accepted by an executor but dropped during shutdown, complete or cancel and release retained budgets/frames without hanging.

On an isolated GPU server, prove a worldgen GPU request is pending, issue /gpur reload while the probe remains active, then prove generation resumes/completes, saves cleanly and matches its saved/reloaded semantic snapshot. A completed-consumption counter alone does not prove in-flight work.

After build-done and immutable JAR freeze, run fresh radius-4 CPU, RTX 3070, GTX 1080 and mixed worlds on loopback port 25620 with a 16 GiB heap; preserve every report and fail closed on mismatch or zero consumed GPU work.
The vanilla worldgen path is integrated end-to-end, runs full required build/tests, and exposes strict verification counters.

The complete required density/noise, aquifer/fluid pressure and surface, feature, lighting and save pipeline is integrated and proven to execute on GPU; backend kernels alone do not satisfy this stage.
Fresh normal world, fixed seed and 4,225-chunk default corpus, vanilla structures on, all requests complete, 16 GiB heap, 0 fallback-only GPU claims.
Fresh world with identical seed/corpus; RTX 3070 admitted and reports accepted vanilla interpolation values with strict CPU parity checks and zero parity failures.
Fresh world with identical seed/corpus; GTX 1080 admitted and reports accepted vanilla interpolation values with strict CPU parity checks and zero parity failures.
Fresh world with identical seed/corpus; both GPUs admitted and both report accepted strict-parity terrain values with zero parity failures.
Each case saves, exits cleanly, restarts, loads every requested chunk with generation disabled, saves again, then matches its pre-restart snapshot.

Every chunk is Status=full and has complete saved-light metadata: isLightOn is present, Starlight light_version matches, and Status is at least LIGHT. Preserve and compare the original isLightOn value because Paper/Starlight may deliberately save false to trigger vanilla relighting. CPU versus every GPU case matches decoded blocks, biomes, all named heightmaps, light flags/arrays, structure starts/references, block entities, entity-store NBT, POI-store NBT and remaining chunk NBT. Require structure starts for the full radius-32 release corpus; a radius-4 smoke may contain zero starts.

A GPU case cannot pass from world equality or CPU fallback. Strict mode requires positive per-device/per-workload deltas for dispatches, acceptedBatches, computedValues, consumedValues and paritySamples on workload boundaries noise 5 and aquifer 6. Verified-exact mode requires positive consumed-work deltas and nonzero absolute startup/periodic parity evidence per selected device/workload; its parity-sample delta may be zero after world-creation warmup. Both modes require accepted terrain interpolation values, zero parity failures and retained fallback-attempt telemetry.

First pass a strict semantic worldgen matrix. Then run separate fresh-world verified-exact matrices on the identical candidate JAR, seed, corpus and worker settings. Report chunks/second with raw per-phase tick-quality artifacts. Only verified-exact timings may report speedup; strict timings include full CPU recomputation and are correctness diagnostics only.

stages.artifact_note: The archived exact 1.0.0 SHA is historical provenance only. Replay its documented scenarios on the new 1.1.0 candidate JAR; do not rebuild or rerun the old artifact as a release gate.
stages.acceptance: On the same immutable 1.1.0 candidate used by all release tests, replay 50/150/300 network-client targets with configured 20% walking (10/30/60 clients), 3,000 AI mobs, redstone fixtures, identical CPU/3070/1080/mixed settings, and retain raw client/server/tick evidence plus server-observed per-client UUID/name, phase sample counts, nonzero from/to displacement and distinct-mover validation.

stages.artifact_note: Historical all-walking failures remain failures; rerun this separate diagnostic on the new 1.1.0 candidate.
stages.acceptance: Keep 300-player all-walking cases separate from the 20%-walking matrix; record watchdog failures as failures and compare against the four known historical exit-70 stalls. Never relabel the prior failures as passes.
Review all artifacts and gate reports; only then change the product version to 2.0.0.

historical_movement_limits: The bot clients implement login/control packets and consume many large world packets as opaque buffers; they are not complete Minecraft clients.

Walkers send grounded position/look packets at 20 Hz around a bounded 2-block-radius route, capped near 2 blocks per second. This tests real network movement callbacks but not ordinary exploration, collision physics, block interaction, combat or inventory use.

movementPackets counts client serialization attempts. Archived 1.0.0 results have only configured walking selection; the fleet's final walking field is 0 because its sampled action is idle after the walking phase. The new candidate GPurBench source now records server-observed per-phase PlayerMoveEvent displacement, but that change is unbuilt and unrun until candidate testing finishes.
The synthetic travel phase is server-directed teleport exploration, not client walking.
historical_workload_limits: The 3,000 fixed cows/zombies have normal AI and activation settings, but invulnerability/persistence and fixture-specific damage/conversion controls alter gameplay; census counts in ticking chunks do not prove every mob's complete AI ran every tick.
Natural-spawn phases vary with mob caps and are not equal-population comparisons.
The 300 redstone circuits exercise CPU updates; they do not establish GPU redstone processing.
